brief.headline: Berry is a trader with a 100% traded revenue mix, so their price carries a reseller margin — benchmark to the maker's price at Bprex (₹1.62/NOS) to eliminate the ₹3.37 L annual excess, but tread carefully: they're in distress (Altman Z -0.18) and losing money (-199.2% net margin), so lead with payment speed and supply security, not a hard squeeze.

priceAsk.summary: Close the ₹3.37 L annual gap to our best price on LDPE bottles by moving from their ₹1.69/NOS to Bprex's maker price of ₹1.62/NOS (4.3% reduction).
priceAsk.target: ₹1.62/NOS for LDPE BOTTLE 5ML WHITE OPAQUE, matching Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited
priceAsk.basis: Berry is 100.0% traded (zero manufactured revenue), so their price includes a reseller margin. We pay ₹1.62/NOS to a direct manufacturer for the same SKU — that's the fair benchmark. The gap costs us ₹3.37 L/yr.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold current 30 Days After Receipt terms; do not extend credit further given their distress position and negative free cash flow of ₹-164.97 Cr.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹6.69 L working capital already tied up at 30 days; extending would worsen our position with a supplier in the distress zone.

brief.financialLeverage: Berry is deeply distressed: net margin -199.2% vs peer median 2.3%, Altman Z score -0.18 (distress zone), debt/equity 220.44x, interest coverage -3.71x, and a Probe42 score of 1/10. They burned ₹-164.97 Cr in free cash flow and posted a ₹-22.50 Cr loss in FY2023-24. Our ₹81.39 L spend represents 7.21% of their ₹11.29 Cr revenue, giving us voice — but pushing too hard risks tipping a fragile supplier. Their 335d cash-conversion cycle (vs 70d peer median) means they value faster payment; offer that in exchange for the price cut rather than demanding both. Lead with supply continuity and a second-source qualification (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) to signal we need reliability, not to threaten.

evidence.point: Berry's revenue is 100% traded (zero manufacturing), so their price embeds a reseller margin that a direct maker does not carry.
We pay ₹1.69/NOS to Berry but only ₹1.62/NOS to Bprex for the same LDPE bottle — a 4.3% gap costing us ₹3.37 L annually.
Berry is loss-making with a net margin of -199.2%, far below the peer median of 2.3%.
Berry's Altman Z score is -0.18, placing them in the distress zone.
Berry's cash-conversion cycle is 335 days, nearly five times the peer median of 70 days, so they value faster cash.
Our ₹81.39 L annual spend is 7.21% of Berry's ₹11.29 Cr revenue, making us a meaningful customer.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100), direct pharma bottle and cap capability — the top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-packaging leader with ₹946.50 Cr revenue and health score B (73/100); strong pharma-bottle fit and financially robust.

alternates.name: Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited
alternates.why: Already our supplier at ₹1.62/NOS for the same LDPE bottle SKU — the price-benchmark and a proven alternate source.

risks: Berry is in the distress zone (Altman Z -0.18) and posted a ₹-22.50 Cr loss in FY2023-24; a hard price squeeze could trigger supply failure — keep Manjushree warm as a backup.
Probe42 financial score is 1/10 and free cash flow is ₹-164.97 Cr — do not increase our concentration here; cap volume and dual-source from day one.
Berry's debt/equity is 220.44x and interest coverage is -3.71x — they are over-leveraged and may not survive another bad year; any concession we win must not come at the cost of continuity.
Their 100% traded model means no manufacturing control — quality or delivery issues will cascade from their upstream supplier, and we have no direct recourse.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we need to talk about two things: first, our ₹1.69/NOS price when we pay ₹1.62/NOS to a direct manufacturer for the same bottle, and second, how we ensure supply continuity given the challenging year you've had — let's find a path that works for both of us.
